draft.title: Religious expression today
card: Many Australians now express spirituality outside traditional institutions such as churches, mosques and temples. They may practise alone, online or in informal groups.
a person who values spiritual ideas or practices, such as meditation or a sense of connection to nature, without belonging to an organised religion.
a religious group that has formed in recent times, often with its own teachings and practices. Some draw on older traditions and some are quite new.
Both trends show that religious expression is changing in form. They do not show that people have stopped seeking meaning.
draft.remember: Spirituality is increasingly expressed outside traditional institutions, and new religious movements are one result of that change.

a.q: Which person is best described as spiritual but not religious?
opts: Sam meditates daily and feels close to nature, with no religion
Priya attends her local temple weekly and follows its teachings
Tom has no interest in spiritual ideas and practises nothing
Lena joined a recent group with its own teachings and leader
a.why: Sam values spiritual practice without belonging to an organised religion. Lena is closer to a new religious movement, because she belongs to a recently formed group with its own teachings.
a.clue: Look for spiritual practice with no organised religion.

b.q: A growing number of people in a Perth suburb join online meditation groups and no longer attend the local church. What does this best show?
opts: Spirituality is being expressed outside institutions
People in the suburb have stopped seeking meaning
Each online group has become a new religious movement
The local church has failed all of its members
b.why: The people still practise spirituality but do so outside a traditional institution. It does not show they have stopped seeking meaning, since meditation is a spiritual practice. Online groups are not automatically new religious movements, which are recently formed religious groups with their own teachings.
b.clue: They have changed where they practise, not whether they practise.
